From 111a12b422a8cfa93deabaef26fec48237163214 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Qi Tang <tpluszz77@gmail.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 00:49:36 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] io_uring/rsrc: reject zero-length fixed buffer import

validate_fixed_range() admits buf_addr at the exact end of the
registered region when len is zero, because the check uses strict
greater-than (buf_end > imu->ubuf + imu->len).  io_import_fixed()
then computes offset == imu->len, which causes the bvec skip logic
to advance past the last bio_vec entry and read bv_offset from
out-of-bounds slab memory.

Return early from io_import_fixed() when len is zero.  A zero-length
import has no data to transfer and should not walk the bvec array
at all.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in io_import_reg_buf+0x697/0x7f0
  Read of size 4 at addr ffff888002bcc254 by task poc/103
  Call Trace:
   io_import_reg_buf+0x697/0x7f0
   io_write_fixed+0xd9/0x250
   __io_issue_sqe+0xad/0x710
   io_issue_sqe+0x7d/0x1100
   io_submit_sqes+0x86a/0x23c0
   __do_sys_io_uring_enter+0xa98/0x1590
  Allocated by task 103:
  The buggy address is located 12 bytes to the right of
   allocated 584-byte region [ffff888002bcc000, ffff888002bcc248)

Fixes: 8622b20f23ed ("io_uring: add validate_fixed_range() for validate fixed buffer")
Signed-off-by: Qi Tang <tpluszz77@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260329164936.240871-1-tpluszz77@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jens Axboe <axboe@kernel.dk>

diff --git a/io_uring/rsrc.c b/io_uring/rsrc.c
index 842e231c8a7c..3f82ed7dd11e 100644
--- a/io_uring/rsrc.c
+++ b/io_uring/rsrc.c
@@ -1062,6 +1062,10 @@ static int io_import_fixed(int ddir, struct iov_iter *iter,
 		return ret;
 	if (!(imu->dir & (1 << ddir)))
 		return -EFAULT;
+	if (unlikely(!len)) {
+		iov_iter_bvec(iter, ddir, NULL, 0, 0);
+		return 0;
+	}
 
 	offset = buf_addr - imu->ubuf;
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `io_uring/rsrc.c`

- **Added early return for zero-length fixed buffer imports**  
  A new conditional block was inserted at the beginning of `io_import_fixed()`, after the initial validation checks but before the offset computation. When the import length `len` is zero, the function now:  
  - Calls `iov_iter_bvec(iter, ddir, NULL, 0, 0)` to initialize the iterator as an empty bvec iterator.  
  - Returns `0` immediately.

## Relationships Between Changes

- The added check prevents the subsequent `buf_addr - imu->ubuf` offset calculation and the bvec-advancement logic from executing when the length is zero. This avoids an out-of-bounds read that occurred because a zero-length import could cause the skip logic to access memory beyond the last valid bvec entry (KASAN slab-out-of-bounds).  
- The change is self-contained within a single file; no other files or functions are modified.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (buf_end > imu->ubuf + imu->len)  // in validate_fixed_range() – allows buf_end == end when len == 0
offset = buf_addr - imu->ubuf;       // offset == imu->len for zero-length at the end
if (offset >= bvec->bv_len) { ... } // skip logic advances bvec past valid entries
```
Reason: `validate_fixed_range()` uses strict greater-than, so it does not reject a buffer address at the exact end of the registered region when `len` is zero. Then `io_import_fixed()` sets `offset` equal to `imu->len` (the full region length), causing the bvec skip logic to advance past the last valid `bio_vec` entry and read `bv_offset` from out-of-bounds slab memory.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (unlikely(!len)) {
    iov_iter_bvec(iter, ddir, NULL, 0, 0);
    return 0;
}
```
Reason: This early return for zero-length imports prevents any access to the bvec array and sets up an empty iov_iter, avoiding the out-of-bounds read entirely.
